Speaking to the Commons for the first time as foreign secretary, Miliband said he would set out measures to prevent UK involvement in projects such as the illegal E1 plan , which critics say would split the West Bank in half. Continue reading...

stories.title: British aid worker mistakenly identified as a survivor of Nepal-Tibet disaster
stories.summary: More than 1,000 people confirmed dead and more than 4,000, including 36 British nationals, remain missing A British aid worker was mistakenly identified by Nepalese authorities as a rescued survivor after returning to Kathmandu on a humanitarian aid flight. Alastair Chambers, a 45-year-old former Gloucester councillor, said he flew to Nepal last week to distribute sleeping bags, food and essentials to communities cut off by collapsed bridges. Continue reading...

stories.title: Relief as five Australians missing in Nepal-Tibet flood disaster found alive
stories.summary: Several missing Australians have been found since Tuesday morning, bringing the total citizens unaccounted for to 38 Australians missing in the Nepal floods: what we know so far A total of five Australians missing after devastating floods ravaged the Nepal-Tibet border last week have been found. Of the five Australians confirmed safe, one was found in Nepal, one in Tibet, and three outside the crisis-hit area. The total number still missing is 38. Continue reading...

stories.title: Japan halves speed limit to 30km/h on all narrow city streets
stories.summary: Speed limit dropped from 60km/h for around 70% of general roads in the hope of making narrow streets of crowded cities safer Drivers on residential roads in Japan have been forced to take their foot off the accelerator, after the speed limit was slashed from 60km/h (37mph) to 30km/h in an attempt to reduce deaths and injuries among pedestrians on narrow urban streets. stories.title: Times Square stabbing: Bank of America vice president named as killed victim
stories.summary: Bank of America executive Erin Piacenti has been named as the victim killed in New York by a woman who stabbed two people in Times Square before being fatally shot by police. The woman has reportedly had a history of mental health issues, according to the NYPD.

stories.title: Death toll passes 1,000 from catastrophic flooding in Nepal and China, officials say
stories.summary: The 26 August disaster began with a chain of events high in the Himalayas. A glacial collapse sent large amounts of rock, ice and meltwater into valleys below, triggering powerful floods downstream.

stories.title: World Nomad Games open in Bishkek before an audience of world leaders
stories.summary: A spectacular performance at the Bishkek Arena opened the sixth edition of the World Nomad Games. This is the biggest competition yet, with more than 100 national teams from every continent. Athletes will compete in 43 disciplines rooted in Asia's ancient nomadic culture.

stories.title: South London Hindu temple prays for missing members after deadly floods in Nepal

stories.summary: Families in Kathmandu post photos of missing relatives after Nepal floods kill more than 1,000 people, with thousands still unaccounted for.

stories.title: Iran says it will return to June ceasefire deal if US does the same
stories.summary: Iran's President Pezeshkian made the offer at the SCO summit in Bishkek hours after Iran and the US exchanged fire over the weekend. IRGC's demands for control of Hormuz and war compensation remain conditions Washington is unlikely to accept.

stories.title: President Tokayev urges ‘concrete initiatives’ as SCO trade nears $1 trillion
stories.summary: The SCO Council of Heads of State met in Bishkek, bringing together leaders of its ten member countries. With SCO trade approaching $1 trillion, Kazakhstan’s President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed new initiatives on security, trade, connectivity and technology.

stories.title: SCO challenges West as diverse group of nations pursues multipolar future
stories.summary: The summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, which represents almost half of the world’s population, ended with an aim to signal the rise of a global powerhouse challenging the West. Yet the SCO's diversity also revealed significant disagreements and divergent interests.

stories.title: Prominent pro-democracy Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong pleads guilty in second national security law case
stories.summary: Wong, already serving prison time for a separate case, pleaded guilty to a second offence under Beijing’s 2020 National Security law, which could see his sentence extended by a minimum of three years and up to life imprisonment.

stories.title: Tyler Robinson pleads not guilty as judge clears path for death penalty in Charlie Kirk assassination case
stories.summary: Robinson, seen as the sole suspect in the 2025 assassination of right-wing activist Charlie Kirk, entered a not guilty plea after a judge gave the green light for prosecutors to advance towards the death penalty as the case goes to trial.

stories.title: Mass burials of unidentified victims continue in Nepal as death toll exceeds 1,100 one week after flash floods
stories.summary: Many were outraged and expressed their disapproval after the government revealed it intended to carry out mass “temporary” burials of the deceased. Nepal’s largely Hindu community objected to the measure which they say goes against religious traditions.

stories.title: Morocco not to blame for Ceuta border breach, says Spanish PM
stories.summary: Pedro Sánchez says two countries cooperating and accuses Israel and Russia of spreading fake news about migration Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has said there is no evidence to suggest the Moroccan government was behind last month’s massive border crossing into Ceuta but accused Israel and Russia of spreading disinformation. stories.summary: Guidance says states must implement ‘comprehensive measures’ to address legacy of racial discrimination A UN committee has said countries are legally obliged to consider reparations for the transatlantic slave trade and take other ⁠measures to address the enduring ⁠legacy of racial ​discrimination. stories.title: Helicopters and boats rescue passengers from capsized ferry in northern Cyprus – video
stories.summary: Passengers of a capsized ship off the coast of Cyprus were seen being rescued by passing vessels and coastguard authorities. Helicopters and boats brought survivors back to shore from the ferry that was carrying about 270 passengers and crew. At least eight people are confirmed to have died and nearly 20 remain missing. Search teams and divers are looking for more survivors in deep waters and it is unclear if people remain trapped on the vessel Nearly 20 people still missing after ferry cap

stories.title: South African airline defends dramatic low-level flyby before rugby union clash
stories.summary: Cape Town stunt sparks major debate over safety risks Airlink insists flyby conducted according to regulations A pre-game stunt involving two passenger jets flying dramatically low over a stadium in South Africa drew huge cheers from the estimated crowd of 56,000 people, but also sparked a major debate over safety risks. The flyby by two Embraer jets, operated by the local airline Airlink, happened on Saturday before the second rugby union Test between South Africa and New Zealand in Cape Town.

stories.title: Flash flood hits Grand Canyon’s Phantom Ranch, more than 20 people missing
stories.summary: Flash flooding near Phantom Ranch sent debris into the Colorado River, destroyed footbridges and left more than 20 people missing or unaccounted for.

stories.title: Michael Jackson fans dance to Thriller to mark King of Pop's 68th birthday
stories.summary: Michaelmania took over the Mexican capital as fans gathered to honour Michael Jackson on what would have been the King of Pop's 68th birthday, performing Thriller’s iconic dance and dressing as zombies.

stories.title: 200 bikers gather at Italy's Castel Gandolfo for motorcycle blessing
stories.summary: Around 200 bikers gathered at Lake Castel Gandolfo for a motorcycle blessing, with Father Tadeusz Rozmus calling for brotherhood, respect and safer roads.

stories.title: Exclusive: US naval blockade is paralysing daily life, Iranians tell Euronews
stories.summary: A Euronews Farsi exclusive shows how a reinstated US naval blockade is paralysing Iran’s trade, driving 70% inflation and pushing families into survival mode. From stranded cargo to empty tables, Iranian citizens speak out on the worsening humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: Algerian president seeks to impose death penalty on arsonists
stories.summary: Algeria declared three days of mourning after wildfires killed 12 people and injured dozens. Authorities said 46 fires remained active, with 54 people hospitalised for burns, including six in critical condition.

stories.title: Eurasian nations gather in Bishkek to forge stronger ties, new alliances
stories.summary: Heads of 21 global and rising powers gather in Bishkek for the SCO summit as wars strain the global order. China and Russia have previously used the SCO to project their influence and their stand against the West, but the middle powers are now there to seek new economic and political momentum.

stories.title: Rybakina tops WTA live rankings as US Open gets underway

stories.title: Jury convicts Duane 'Keffe D' Davis of first degree murder in 1996 killing of hip-hop icon Tupac Shakur
stories.summary: The verdict lays to rest decades of speculation and conspiracy from avid hip-hop fans around the world in the high-profile killing that went unresolved for close to 30 years. Davis is expected to appeal the conviction.

stories.title: US teen charged with aiding San Diego mosque shooters share livestream and manifesto
stories.summary: Sarah Santiago, 17, will be charged as an adult, according to a press release issued by prosecutor James O'Neill's office.

stories.title: Norwegians pay tribute to 'grandfather figure' King Harald V – video

Mourners gathered to lay floral tributes after news of his death. Norway’s prime minister, Jonas Gahr Støre, also paid tribute to King Harald, saying the 'entire nation is in mourning'. stories.title: Michael Jordan's 1998 NBA Finals sneakers sell for a record $2.2 million
stories.summary: In 1998, Michael Jordan laced up a pair of his iconic black and red Air Jordan 13s to bring home a Bulls victory during Game 2 of his final NBA championship — and now they are the most expensive sneakers ever to sell at auction. The game-winning sneakers sold for $2.2 million at Sotheby's in New York on Tuesday, smashing the sneaker auction record of $1.47 million, set in 2021 by a pair of Nike Air Ships that Jordan wore earlier in his career.
